newsitem.title: USA: United Tech unit silent on layoff report.
newsitem.headline: United Tech unit silent on layoff report.

text.p: Aircraft engine-maker Pratt & Whitney, a unit of United Technologies Corp, declined comment Thursday on a published report that it plans to cut 2,500 white-collar workers worldwide by the end of this month.
"We never comment on rumors and speculation," Pratt spokesman Mark Sullivan told Reuters.
A story in the Manchester, Conn., Journal Inquirer, quoting unnamed Pratt sources, said layoffs would include 1,500 workers in Connecticut.
It said the layoffs were dictated by parent United Technologies, which wants Pratt to slash about $250 million in costs.
At least 500 of the job cuts would be at Pratt's headquarters in East Hartford, the newspaper said.
Pratt has already slashed its workforce in response to defense-industry cutbacks in recent years. Its worldwide workforce is now 30,000, down from 42,000 in 1993.
Its Connecticut workforce has shrunk to 12,000 from 23,000 over the same period, Sullivan said.
